transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood Solutions), Lena (AtlasPoint CISO), Markus (VP Eng), Priya (SecOps), Diego (Infra)

Summary: quick security intake to validate hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), verify SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC model, audit logs, and encryption/KMS details. Customer is leaning Private/Dedicated for PII-heavy workloads; timeline compressed (Q1 pilot).

Topics: SOC2 & ISO status, SSO/SAML integration, SSO provisioning, RBAC scopes, audit log retention and export, KMS provider and envelope encryption, data residency and retention windows, network egress, POC plan and success criteria.

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time, um quick intro from our side, I'm Maya Chen, account exec for Redwood inference, with me is Ravi Patel our SE and Noah who does solutions.
[00:12] Lena: hi, this is Lena. I'm CISO at AtlasPoint. we wanted a security-first call. we have some PII workflows so we'll need strong assurances.
[00:18] Markus: Markus here, VP Eng, i'll be in as well to talk infra constraints.
[00:22] Priya: priya (secops) joining too. lots of questions about keys and audit.
[00:26] Maya: awesome, we'll jump in. first high level, can you share what you've already validated? what audits do you need from vendors?
[00:33] Lena: sure. short answer: SOC2 type II is mandatory, ISO 27001 nice-to-have. we audit vendors quarterly, we need attestation, and we also need runtime audit logs forwarded to our SIEM for 90 days. retention beyond that is negotiable.
[00:46] Markus: and network wise we run in GCP with VPC peering to some partners, we try to avoid public internet egress for tokens.
[00:54] Maya: ok makes sense. Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — briefly: hosted is fastest but multi-tenant, dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our infra, private is customer VPC or on-prem with our private control plane. do you have a preferred mode?
[01:09] Priya: we're leaning private for sensitive models. dedicated could be acceptable if we can get VPC-level isolation and bring-your-own-key.
[01:17] Ravi: got it. we do have BYOK options via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. quick caveat: hosted has a dedicated encryption-at-rest but not BYOK by default unless under an enterprise add-on.
[01:31] Diego: can you clarify BYOK? do we manage the keys entirely or do you hold a wrapper?
[01:36] Ravi: you can either provide keys via your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we use envelope encryption; with Private, keys live in your account, we don't persist plaintext. with Dedicated we can arrange a customer-controlled KMS depending on contract.
[01:50] Lena: that matters. we have strict rotation (30 days) and require HSM-backed keys.
[01:55] Maya: noted. we'll verify HSM compliance in the SOC2 artifacts.
[01:58] [background murmur]
[02:05] Markus: audit logs — we need per-request logs with caller identity and model/version, ideally streamed to our SIEM (Splunk). retention target initially 90 days, with archives for 2 years. any blockers?
[02:18] Ravi: we emit structured audit logs for every request — model, route, token counts, latencies, user id when provided. we can stream via secure syslog or push to customer S3/GCS buckets, or push to Splunk HTTP Event Collector. export cadence and encryption-in-flight are supported.
[02:35] Priya: do logs include full prompts? because of PII we prefer redaction or only metadata.
[02:41] Ravi: great question. we have config to redact or hash prompt payloads before shipping; you can also keep full logs on-prem in Private mode so they never traverse our hosted control plane.
[02:53] Lena: valuable. about SSO — we use Okta. we need SAML SSO, provisioning via SCIM, and granular RBAC. can Redwood do SAML + SCIM?
[03:03] Maya: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported. RBAC is role- and tag-based; you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles (admin, dev, read-only, billing).
[03:14] Markus: we need separation: devs can call hosted endpoints for testing but only the production model variants should be callable by prod service accounts. can you do model-level permissions?
[03:25] Ravi: yes, fine-grained permissions exist — you can lock models and routes behind roles or service accounts. we also support token-level restrictions and per-route quotas.
[03:34] Priya: about SAML asserts — we need signed assertions and short session TTLs.
[03:39] Maya: supported. session TTLs can be configured and assertions must be signed; we'll share the SAML metadata endpoint and the SCIM schema.
[03:47] Lena: data residency — some datasets must remain in EU. do you have region pinning for inference?
[03:53] Ravi: yes. routing policies let you pin to region clusters. Private deployment in an EU VPC keeps data in-region. hosted endpoints are region-aware but multi-region fallback exists if capacity is constrained — we can disable cross-region fallback for strict residency.
[04:08] Markus: performance question: we need consistent latency under 200ms 95p for short prompts; any guarantees?
[04:14] Maya: for Dedicated we can commit to latency SLOs in contract. Hosted is best-effort but we publish performance profiles. Dedicated and Private give more predictability because you control capacity.
[04:26] Diego: cost tradeoff — curious about encryption CPU overhead for on-prem and any added latency with BYOK.
[04:32] Ravi: encryption overhead is negligible for per-request symmetric ops; KMS envelope unwrap does add a small one-time cost per key rotation or when retrieving ephemeral DEKs. we cache DEKs and use hardware acceleration where available. we can add numbers in a follow-up doc.
[04:49] [crosstalk]
[05:00] Lena: legal/regulatory — we need vendor contractual language for data processing, breach notification timelines, and subprocessor list.
[05:07] Maya: we have standard DPA and subprocessors list; breach notification windows in enterprise plans are 72 hours and we can negotiate SLA-backed timelines for Dedicated/Private.
[05:17] Priya: retention policy — we need a default data retention for logs (90 days), model traces 30 days unless flagged for investigations. can Redwood separate logs vs payloads?
[05:28] Ravi: yes. logs, traces, and training traces are separable. we can configure auto-delete rules and TTLs per tenant. for Private, you control retention in your environment.
[05:37] Markus: about evals — we may run synthetic tests with PHI-like tokens; is there an isolated test channel?
[05:44] Ravi: yes, we recommend using a dedicated namespace in Dedicated or Private. Hosted has sandboxing but not fully isolated compute.
[05:50] Lena: compliance artifacts: we need SOC2, ISO cert copies, penetration test summaries, and your KMS architecture diagram.
[05:58] Maya: we'll attach SOC2 type II report and pen test summary. note: some pen test details are redacted but we can provide an executive summary.
[06:08] Priya: one more: key rotation — we require 30 day rotations and proof of rotation logs. can Redwood show rotation audit?
[06:15] Ravi: rotation events are logged and we can surface them in audit streams. for BYOK where the key is in your KMS, rotation is under your control — we surface only the envelope ops.
[06:27] [pause]
[06:32] Markus: timeline — we'd like a Q1 pilot, two-week POC, then scale if results satisfactory. is that realistic?
[06:40] Maya: yes, that's doable. typical POC: 2-4 weeks depending on scope. we'll propose a minimal test plan: anonymized test dataset, latency and cost measurements, and security checklist verification.
[06:52] Lena: success criteria: no PII leakage in logs, audit stream to our SIEM, SSO + SCIM integration with Okta, BYOK with HSM-backed keys, and a plan for region pinning.
[07:06] Ravi: i'll draft the POC checklist. can we get a list of sample prompts and traffic shape?
[07:11] Markus: yes, we'll share traffic profile and representative prompts, stripped of real PHI.
[07:17] Maya: great. next up i'll send the SOC2 doc and network diagram. Ravi will follow with a Private vs Dedicated sizing + cost delta and a POC checklist.
[07:28] Priya: also, can you share your audit log schema? we need to map fields to Splunk indexing.
[07:34] Ravi: yes, will include example JSON events for the logs.
[07:38] Lena: any competitors you think we should benchmark? we evaluated Anthropic and AWS Bedrock quickly, but their managed options didn't offer the same BYOK or on-prem route without heavy engineering.
[07:50] Maya: understood. We'll include a short comparison note in the follow-up.
[07:55] [audio glitch, few seconds lost]
[08:05] Diego: quick nit: for Private deployment, what's the control plane visibility — do you still have telemetry to our control plane?
[08:11] Ravi: Private installs optional control-plane connectors. we can run a completely air-gapped runtime while keeping a local control plane; or you can opt for a managed control plane in your VPC that gives us minimal telemetry only if you consent.
[08:27] Lena: final question: can Redwood provide SOC2 scoping details on subprocessors and subcontractors? we need names and locations.
[08:35] Maya: yes, subprocessors list provided, with geographies. will include in the packet.
[08:40] Priya: thanks all — anything else?
[08:43] Maya: quick recap — we'll send SOC2 + pen test summary, network diagram, sample audit logs; Ravi will prep POC checklist and sizing; AtlasPoint to provide KMS vendor details + sample prompts. target dates in next_steps.
[08:56] Lena: sounds good. talk soon.

[End of meeting — rough transcription, some segments may be noisy or mis-typed by auto-transcription.]
